messages:
Anya: heads-up — since the kernel flip yesterday we're seeing oscillating p95 latency on the microbatch path. looks like coalesce windows are self-synchronizing and creating microbursts. anyone else? :thinking:
Jia: saw the alert, digging in. preliminary: KV hit-rate dropped ~6% for mid-tail requests right after the deploy. batch sizes vary wildly (1 -> 12) for same arrival pattern.
Marco: that smells like batching + kernel dispatch hysteresis. new kernels favor longer sequences; scheduler seems to wait for token_budget_target but jitter is too small so queues align.
Anya: attaching profiler snapshot + quick metrics:
```
profile: run-224999-15m
p50: 28ms p95: 180ms p99: 420ms
throughput: 12k tokens/s
avg_batch_size: 4.1
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.72 -> baseline 0.78
kernel_swap_time: 4.2ms (spikes up to 12ms during coalesce events)
batch_formation_skew: stdev=3.8ms
```
Jia: thanks. I also pulled sampling traces — kernel selection sometimes triggers a small synchronous allocator path when occupancy flips across threshold. that adds ~6-10ms tail.
Lucy: idea: add randomized jitter proportional to arrival variance instead of fixed jitter_pct. make jitter = min(10ms, 0.2 * interarrival_std). should decrease alignment.
Marco: agree. also propose tiny hysteresis on kernel routing: require occupancy change > 30% sustained for 50ms before switching kernels. removes flip-flop.
Anya: rough config proposal to test in canary (Dedicated pool):
```
serve.continuous_batching:
  micro_batch_ms: 6  # was 3
  coalesce_delay_us: 1200  # was 800
  jitter_strategy: dynamic_std  # enable Lucy's dynamic jitter
  jitter_max_ms: 10
  token_budget_target: 180  # slightly lower to favor stable occupancy
  kernel_hysteresis_ms: 50
  kernel_hysteresis_pct: 0.3
```
Sam: can run a 4-hour canary on a small dedicated shard. want me to include a traffic replay (prod-10%) or synthetic Poisson?
Jia: both — replay for realistic KV patterns + poisson for stress. include the previous kernel version as fallback.
Marco: add metric exports: batch_occupancy_histogram, kernel_switch_count, coalesce_alignment_index (measure of how many requests arrive within +/- jitter window).
perf-bot: ALERT: deploy/224998 -> 224999 kernel-update increased kernel_switch_count by 3.8x over 30m, correlated with p95 spike. See /observability/alerts/224999-kernel-flap.
Lucy: small experiment we can run quickly — keep micro_batch_ms=6 but set coalesce_delay_us to 600 with dynamic jitter. hypothesis: shorter coalesce but higher jitter will keep batch sizes but reduce alignment. if hit_rate still low then raise micro_batch_ms.
Anya: good plan. action items:
- Sam: start canary with replay + poisson, include old kernel fallback (ETA 30m)
- Jia: add temporary probe metrics (occupancy_hist, align_index) and enable sampling profiler at 0.1%
- Marco: implement kernel hysteresis toggle in scheduler (feature flag)
- Lucy: add dynamic jitter function to runtime config + small unit tests
I'll collect results after 4h and post a summary. if p95 drops < baseline+10% and kv_hit recovers we can roll fix. :thumbsup:
Sam: started canary job id=cascade-canary-224999. replay at 10% + poisson at 1k rps for 30m ramp. logs streaming: https://internal/logs/cascade-canary-224999
Jia: profiler snapshot after 20m of canary attached in the logs — early sign: kernel_switch_count down 65% with hysteresis enabled, batch_stdev -> 1.2ms, kv_hit up 3%. still watching tail.
Anya: perfect. please ping me if p99 > 400ms. I'll hold on rolling the kernel globally until we confirm.
Marco: when we stabilise, follow-up: consider adaptive token_budget_target that nudges based on short-term kv_hit and occupancy to make the scheduler proactive.
Lucy: noted for Optimize backlog. also adding a small doc snippet to explain dynamic jitter math.
perf-bot: RESOLVED: cascade-canary-224999 shows p95 back within 8% of baseline after hysteresis+jitter changes.
Anya: closing loop — great work team. will file an RFC for the adaptive token budget change and scheduler hysteresis as next steps.
